abstract: ArXiv:2606.30783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify a security-fidelity tradeoff in defending LLMs against indirect prompt injection: defenses resist injected instructions largely by suppressing untrusted text, which corrupts tasks that must preserve it, such as translation and document editing. Attack-success metrics cannot see this, because a model that ignores an injection and one that faithfully processes it as data score identically. We introduce SecFid, a benchmark built so that executing an injection, processing it as data, and ignoring it produce distinguishable outputs. This makes fidelity measurable and exposes a frontier: across 1,168 examples and 48 configurations, no model or defense achieves both objectives. The highest-fidelity model reaches 96.5% fidelity at 47.8% security, while the most secure defenses invert this, at 99.3% security but only 71.0%-73.9% fidelity. Even defenses with identical security differ in how they earn it: some repair hijacks into faithful processing, others simply suppress benign content. A decision-theoretic analysis shows why no fixed choice can be right everywhere: the correct behavior is not a property of the defense but of the deployment, set by its relative cost of a hijack versus a dropped span. Security alone therefore measures only half of robustness, and reporting it without fidelity hides the price at which it was bought.
tldr: This paper identifies a security-fidelity tradeoff in defending LLMs against indirect prompt injection, showing that defenses that suppress untrusted text harm tasks requiring faithful text preservation.
motivation: Current attack-success metrics fail to capture fidelity loss when defenses suppress benign content, hiding the true cost of security.
method: The authors introduce SecFid, a benchmark that distinguishes between executing an injection, processing it as data, and ignoring it, enabling measurement of both security and fidelity across 1,168 examples and 48 configurations.
result: No model or defense achieves both high security and high fidelity; the highest-fidelity model reaches 96.5% fidelity at 47.8% security, while the most secure defenses achieve 99.3% security but only 71.0%-73.9% fidelity.
conclusion: Security alone is insufficient; reporting fidelity is necessary to understand the true robustness of defenses, and the optimal behavior depends on deployment-specific costs.

title: AI-Generated PowerShell Malware: An Experimental Framework And Dataset
authors: Luciano Pianese, Vittorio Orbinato, Pietro Liguori, Roberto Natella
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI has emerged as a significant cybersecurity threat, with several recent attack campaigns leveraging LLMs to generate code for malicious purposes via scripting languages such as PowerShell. Consequently, for cybersecurity analysts, it is imperative to investigate the offensive capabilities of AI code generators. In this paper, we propose an experimental framework to assess LLM-generated PowerShell malware, which comprises a novel sandbox approach for dynamic analysis of AI-generated malware. Furthermore, we present a novel, manually curated dataset of real-world PowerShell malware, annotated in natural language to assist the training and evaluation of LLMs. Finally, this study evaluates permissive, open-weight LLMs adapted to PowerShell malware generation. Our results reveal a high degree of similarity between real malware and LLM-generated ones in terms of triggered OS malicious events, with a median Jaccard index of 84.5% and 48.4% of instances achieving complete overlap.
tldr: This paper presents an experimental framework and dataset for analyzing AI-generated PowerShell malware, focusing on cybersecurity threats from LLMs.
motivation: Generative AI poses a cybersecurity threat as LLMs can generate malicious code; analysts need tools to assess offensive capabilities of AI code generators.
method: The authors propose a sandbox approach for dynamic analysis of AI-generated PowerShell malware and create a manually curated dataset of real-world PowerShell malware annotated in natural language.
result: LLM-generated malware shows high similarity to real malware in triggered OS events, with median Jaccard index of 84.5% and 48.4% instances achieving complete overlap.
conclusion: The framework and dataset enable evaluation of LLM-generated malware, highlighting the need for defenses against AI-generated cyber threats.

title: Automated Reasoning With Nested Datatypes
authors: Tomer Hakak, Yoni Zohar, Andrew Reynolds, Clark Barrett, Cesare Tinelli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a theory of nested datatypes. The theory is obtained by restricting the naive combination of datatypes and arrays, so as to prevent non-standard models from emerging. A decision procedure for the theory is given and proven correct. Finally, we describe an implementation of the procedure, as well as an evaluation over both real-world and crafted benchmarks.
tldr: This paper introduces a theory of nested datatypes and a decision procedure for it, with an implementation and evaluation.
motivation: The naive combination of datatypes and arrays leads to non-standard models; a restricted theory is needed to avoid this.
method: A theory of nested datatypes is defined by restricting the combination of datatypes and arrays, and a decision procedure is proven correct.
result: The decision procedure is implemented and evaluated on real-world and crafted benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed theory and decision procedure effectively handle nested datatypes without non-standard models.

title: Curvature-Guided Module Localization For Low-Rank Detoxification Of Backdoored Large Language Models
authors: Arash Raftari, Mehrdad Mahdavi, Nathan Blackthorn, Andrew Arash Mahyari
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to large language models (LLMs) by causing otherwise benign systems to produce attacker-specified malicious behavior when a hidden trigger is present. In this work, we study post hoc detoxification of backdoored LLMs in a practical setting where the defender has access to the poisoned model but does not wish to retrain the full network from scratch. We propose a mechanistically guided weight-space repair framework that first localizes modules involved in propagating trigger-induced behavior using activation patching and Fisher/K-FAC curvature analysis, and then applies targeted low-rank repair to only the most influential modules. We evaluate the method on poisoned variants of with triggers inserted at the beginning, middle, and end of otherwise benign prompts. Results show that the proposed approach substantially suppresses trigger-conditioned malicious responses while preserving benign model behavior. These findings suggest that backdoor removal in LLMs can be formulated as a localized structural repair problem rather than only a broad behavioral alignment problem.
tldr: This paper proposes a curvature-guided module localization method for low-rank detoxification of backdoored large language models.
motivation: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to LLMs, and existing detoxification methods often require full retraining or are not targeted.
method: The method uses activation patching and Fisher/K-FAC curvature analysis to localize modules involved in trigger-induced behavior, then applies targeted low-rank repair to those modules.
result: The approach substantially suppresses trigger-conditioned malicious responses while preserving benign model behavior.
conclusion: Backdoor removal in LLMs can be formulated as a localized structural repair problem rather than only a broad behavioral alignment problem.

title: Secure-CHG: A Comprehensive Framework For Robust And Fair Federated Learning Via Hybrid Defense And Contribution-Aware Trust
authors: Guanming Che, Qiang Wang, Jian Xu, Fucai Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is highly susceptible to stealthy backdoor attacks, which aim to force a model into predicting an attacker-chosen target class for inputs containing a specific trigger. However, existing statistical defenses primarily focus on the early stages of model convergence. In this paper, we identify a fundamental vulnerability termed ``Late-stage Failure.'' We demonstrate that as the global model converges, decaying gradient norms render malicious and benign updates morphologically indistinguishable. This vanishing statistical variance effectively blinds traditional defenses, enabling adaptive adversaries to remain dormant and subsequently hijack the training process. To overcome these constraints, we propose Secure-CHG, a hybrid framework that pivots the defense paradigm from superficial morphological detection toward intrinsic semantic contribution verification. Secure-CHG employs an adaptive defense pipeline: a cascaded statistical filter stabilizes optimization during the early oscillatory phase, while a novel CHG-Shapley mechanism takes over during late-stage convergence. By leveraging sample hardness (i.e., local training loss) to project updates into a composite Hardness-Gradient space, it effectively amplifies adversarial semantic traces, enabling the isolation of stealthy attackers even as gradient norms vanish. Furthermore, we derive a closed-form solution for CHG-Shapley, facilitating low-complexity, retraining-free node valuation and trust-modulated aggregation. Extensive evaluations on CIFAR-10, MedMNIST, and NEU-SDDB demonstrate that Secure-CHG effectively mitigates Late-stage Failure. Specifically, it significantly suppresses advanced backdoor attacks, reducing their attack success rate by 2.3[MATH] and 2.0[MATH] relative to the mainstream Krum and Trimmed Mean baselines, respectively.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning defense framework against backdoor attacks, focusing on late-stage convergence vulnerabilities.
motivation: Federated learning is vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and existing defenses fail during late-stage convergence when gradient norms vanish.
method: Secure-CHG uses a cascaded statistical filter for early stages and a CHG-Shapley mechanism for late-stage detection, leveraging sample hardness to amplify adversarial traces.
result: Experiments on CIFAR-10, MedMNIST, and NEU-SDDB show Secure-CHG reduces attack success rate by 2.3× and 2.0× compared to Krum and Trimmed Mean baselines.
conclusion: The hybrid defense effectively mitigates late-stage backdoor attacks in federated learning.

title: Beyond But-for Test: Counterfactual Explanation In Abstract Argumentation Via Actual Causality (Extended Version)
authors: Siyi Liu, Muyun Shao, Beishui Liao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counterfactual explanation in abstract argumentation calls for an answer to the what-if query: would the topic argument still be accepted if the status of certain other arguments were changed? Existing approaches are limited to the but-for test and fail to accommodate more refined counterfactual conditions. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an intervention-based counterfactual reasoning framework in abstract argumentation. Our approach encodes the acceptance conditions of arguments as equations, then defines an intervention operator that supports (1) changing sets of arguments simultaneously, and (2) fixing witness arguments to their actual labels. Guided by the refined counterfactual condition introduced in the Halpern-Pearl definition, our method goes beyond the but-for test, thereby correctly identifying causes in argumentation structures such as Preemption and Overdetermination. Through comparison, we show that our method surpasses prior methods in both expressiveness and reliability.
tldr: This paper proposes a counterfactual explanation framework in abstract argumentation using actual causality, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Existing counterfactual explanations in abstract argumentation are limited to the but-for test and fail to handle refined conditions like preemption and overdetermination.
method: The authors encode argument acceptance conditions as equations and define an intervention operator that supports changing sets of arguments and fixing witness arguments, guided by the Halpern-Pearl definition of actual causality.
result: The proposed method surpasses prior methods in expressiveness and reliability, correctly identifying causes in argumentation structures such as Preemption and Overdetermination.
conclusion: The intervention-based framework provides a more refined counterfactual reasoning approach for abstract argumentation.

title: Probe Choice Changes Canary-Memorization Verdicts: Three Post-Hoc Disagreement Case Studies In A Text-Dominant LoRA-Tuned Autoregressive Testbed
authors: Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang, Yanhang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We audit a fixed prefix-window mean-NLL memorization probe (K=20) on a Qwen2.5-VL-7B canary testbed and report three post-hoc cases where it disagrees with full-span secret NLL or greedy exact-recall. C3 (false negative, window truncation): damage lands on hex tokens outside K=20; the probe stays flat while hit@1 drops. C4 (false positive, non-secret drift): the probe moves, but approximately 99% sits on non-secret preamble; the secret span and hit@1 are unchanged. C5 (ambiguous in-window drop): the probe falls on an undertrained baseline while full-span hex is positive and hit@1=0. Recommendation: report (i) full-span secret NLL, (ii) a span-localised decomposition, (iii) behavioural exact-recall at k>=4, and (iv) decoy probes before asserting secret-specificity. Evidence is on controlled canaries in one backbone; magnitudes are testbed-specific.
tldr: This paper audits a memorization probe on a vision-language model and finds disagreements with other metrics, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The authors aim to evaluate the reliability of a specific memorization probe in detecting canary memorization in a text-dominant LoRA-tuned autoregressive model.
method: They compare a fixed prefix-window mean-NLL probe with full-span secret NLL and greedy exact-recall on a Qwen2.5-VL-7B canary testbed, analyzing three post-hoc disagreement cases.
result: They identify three cases: false negative due to window truncation, false positive due to non-secret drift, and ambiguous in-window drop, showing that probe choice can change memorization verdicts.
conclusion: They recommend reporting multiple metrics including full-span secret NLL, span-localized decomposition, behavioral exact-recall, and decoy probes before asserting secret-specificity.

title: Securing The Ai Agent: A Unified Framework For Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming
authors: Yong Yang, Xing Zheng, Huiyu Wu, Huangsheng Cheng, Xiaorong Shi, Jing Guo, Bo Yang, Yi Zhou, Xiangfan Wu, Zonghao Ying
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fast growth of open-source AI infrastructure, from model serving engines and agent platforms to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem and the language models themselves, has outpaced the security tooling available to defend it. We present AI-Infra-Guard, an open-source framework that organizes AI red teaming around a single observation: the attack surface of an AI agent is stratified across layers (infrastructure, protocol/tool, agent behavior, and model), and no single detection paradigm fits all of them. The framework therefore matches a paradigm to each layer, from deterministic rule matching over 75+ AI components and 1{,}400+ vulnerability rules, through LLM-driven agentic auditing of MCP servers and agent-skill packages and multi-turn black-box agent red teaming, to a jailbreak harness with 26+ attack operators over sixteen datasets. To our knowledge it is the only open-source framework to span all of these, including supply-chain auditing of the agent skills that increasingly extend AI agents. We release AI-Infra-Guard as open source so that can serve as a practical foundation for agent security and a shared base for the community to build on.
tldr: This paper presents a unified framework for red-teaming AI agents across multiple security layers.
motivation: The rapid growth of open-source AI infrastructure has outpaced security tooling, necessitating a comprehensive red-teaming framework.
method: The framework stratifies the attack surface into infrastructure, protocol/tool, agent behavior, and model layers, and applies tailored detection paradigms (rule matching, LLM-driven auditing, multi-turn black-box testing, jailbreak harness) to each.
result: The framework covers over 75 AI components and 1,400+ vulnerability rules, and includes supply-chain auditing for agent skills.
conclusion: AI-Infra-Guard is the first open-source framework to span all these layers, providing a practical foundation for agent security.

title: The Decomposition Is The Fingerprint: Per-Component Identity For Agent Skills
authors: Hongliang Liu, Yuhao Wu, Tung-Ling Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents increasingly acquire and execute skills at runtime: bundles of prompt instructions, executable code, and tool declarations fetched from marketplaces and other agents. Governing them needs a stable notion of skill identity, yet cryptographic hashing is engineered to destroy the very similarity we need, as a one-character edit scrambles the digest. We present a compact, locality-sensitive fingerprint that embeds each component of a skill and projects it to bits with a multi-bank SimHash, giving a fixed 120-byte signature compared in constant time by Hamming distance. Our central claim is that keeping the fingerprint as a per-component triple (prompt, code, tools), rather than a single score, is what makes it useful: the triple recovers skill-family identity through paraphrase, renaming, refactoring, and controlled code translation when another component remains shared, while independent multilingual reimplementation is not recovered; it also localizes which component carries the reuse. We claim lineage, not behavioral equivalence: identity supplies the structural axis of a registry and leaves safety to behavioral verification. The fingerprint reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.974 (95% CI [0.956, 0.994]) over 4,950 pairwise comparisons while using 77x fewer bits than the embedding it approximates, with ranking preserved in expectation and finite-bit concentration; the per-component split turns one number into relationship classification, families, novelty, and a portable "SkillBOM" for a skill registry. On a 906-skill injection benchmark the fingerprint recognizes injected skills as tampered copies of a known base and localizes the change, but recognition is not trust: it remains, by design, an identity signal complementary to behavioral verification rather than a safety verdict.
tldr: The paper proposes a locality-sensitive fingerprint for AI agent skills to enable similarity detection and lineage tracking, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: AI agents need a stable notion of skill identity for governance, but cryptographic hashing destroys similarity information.
method: A multi-bank SimHash generates a 120-byte fingerprint per skill component (prompt, code, tools), compared by Hamming distance.
result: The fingerprint achieves AUC 0.974 on pairwise comparisons, uses 77x fewer bits than embeddings, and localizes changes in injected skills.
conclusion: The fingerprint provides a structural identity signal for skill registries, complementary to behavioral verification.

title: Learning Fair Allocation Of Indivisible Items From Limited Feedback
authors: Xinyu Liu, David Kempe, Evi Micha
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a setting in which an algorithm must output a fair allocation of indivisible items while "learning on the job". More specifically, the algorithm is to output an allocation satisfying EF1, PROP1, or similar fairness notions; however, the algorithm initially has no information about the agents' valuations, and can only learn about them by (repeatedly) proposing an allocation, and obtaining feedback about a fairness violation in the allocation. Importantly, the observed fairness violation may be adversarially chosen. The algorithm's goal is to converge to a fair allocation in rounds polynomial in the number of agents and items, ideally with only polynomial computation. We prove two main results: first, when the valuations are additive, then even for mixed items (goods and chores), an allocation satisfying EF1 or PROP1 can be found in polynomial time using the corresponding feedback. These results are instantiations of a more general framework which maintains a polytope of candidate valuations consistent with all past feedback. The algorithm repeatedly constructs putative valuations and uses them to propose allocations; the observed violations then define separating hyperplanes, allowing the algorithm to emulate the ellipsoid method. When the valuations are monotone, we present an algorithm which is guaranteed to find an EF1 allocation in polynomially many iterations; however, its internal calculations are not guaranteed to be polynomial. The algorithm again maintains putative valuations, and only considers allocations in which each agent obtains an interval plus one additional item with respect to an arbitrary ordering of the items. We (non-constructively) prove that there always exist EF1 allocations of this form, allowing us to use a further generalization of the preceding ellipsoid-based ideas.
tldr: This paper studies learning fair allocations of indivisible items from limited feedback, focusing on EF1 and PROP1 notions.
motivation: The algorithm must output a fair allocation without prior knowledge of agent valuations, learning only through feedback on proposed allocations.
method: The algorithm maintains a polytope of candidate valuations consistent with feedback, uses the ellipsoid method to converge to a fair allocation.
result: For additive valuations, an EF1 or PROP1 allocation can be found in polynomial time; for monotone valuations, an EF1 allocation is guaranteed in polynomially many iterations but with potentially non-polynomial internal computation.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical guarantees for learning fair allocations under limited feedback, but is not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Cve-ttp Kg: Knowledge Graph Linking Software Vulnerabilities To Attack Behaviors
authors: Basant Agarwal, Dincy R. Arikkat, Swati Yadav, Serena Nicolazzo, Antonino Nocera, Vinod P
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the evolving threat landscape, adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to launch sophisticated attacks, challenging traditional defenses. Although databases like CVE and NVD provide detailed technical information, they often lack links to attacker behaviors such as tactics and techniques, limiting effective threat interpretation and response. This work bridges this gap by connecting vulnerabilities with behavioral patterns from the MITRE ATT&CK framework. We construct a CVE-TTP Knowledge Graph that links CVEs to tactics and techniques using classification and relation extraction. Transformer-based models are developed for behavior identification, with CySecBERT achieving macro F1-scores of 87.71% (techniques) and 96.16% (tactics). Also, we created an annotated dataset with 24,820 entities and 43,608 relations for entity and relation extraction. The pipeline-based approach achieves macro F1-scores of 0.86 (entity extraction) and 0.99 (relation extraction), while a span-based joint model achieves 0.78. These outputs are integrated into a Neo4j-based Cyber Threat Knowledge Graph, enabling structured visualization of vulnerabilities.
tldr: This paper constructs a knowledge graph linking software vulnerabilities (CVEs) to attacker behaviors (MITRE ATT&CK) using NLP and relation extraction.
motivation: Traditional vulnerability databases lack connections to attacker tactics and techniques, hindering threat interpretation and response.
method: Transformer-based models (CySecBERT) classify CVEs into tactics/techniques; pipeline and joint models extract entities and relations to build a Neo4j knowledge graph.
result: CySecBERT achieves macro F1-scores of 87.71% for techniques and 96.16% for tactics; entity extraction F1=0.86, relation extraction F1=0.99.
conclusion: The CVE-TTP knowledge graph effectively links vulnerabilities to attack behaviors, enabling structured threat analysis.

title: Comparative Analysis Of Machine Learning Based Intrusion Detection In Realistic IoT Networks
authors: Chuadhry Mujeeb Ahmed Rana Alharbi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly growing and expanding into various sectors, such as healthcare, transportation, smart homes, and more. Despite the benefits of using IoT devices, they present several challenges. Given the significant role these devices play in our lives, it is crucial to address issues related to their security and privacy. These devices are limited in resources, which complicates their security and the protection of the data that they manage. The paper aims to examine intrusion detection systems using the Gotham2025 dataset, generated through the Gotham testbed, which consists of 78 emulated IoT devices utilising various protocols, including MQTT, CoAP, and RTSP, to assist in safeguarding IoT networks from attacks. We conduct a comparative analysis between five machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and Deep Neural Network. We demonstrate that the Random Forest Classifier was the top-performing model, achieving an F1-score of 0.99 in classifying attacks.
tldr: This paper compares machine learning algorithms for intrusion detection in IoT networks using the Gotham2025 dataset.
motivation: IoT devices are resource-constrained and vulnerable to attacks, necessitating effective intrusion detection systems.
method: Five machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Deep Neural Network) are evaluated on the Gotham2025 dataset from a testbed of 78 emulated IoT devices.
result: Random Forest achieved the highest F1-score of 0.99 in classifying attacks.
conclusion: Machine learning, particularly Random Forest, can effectively detect intrusions in IoT networks.

title: Robocalls: A Worldwide Or US-only Problem? Analyzing Spam And Fraud In International Phone Calls
authors: Kemal Altwlkany, Andro Mer\'cep, Tomislav {\dj}uri\v{c}i\'c, Ante Kapetanovi\'c, Emanuel Lacic
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unsolicited automated phone calls (robocalls) are a serious threat: in the US alone, these calls resulted in reported losses of 1.1$ billion during 2025. Phishing and spoofing consistently rank among the most reported crimes within the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center, with phone call scams having the highest reported median loss. Combating robocalls is difficult due to many legal and practical constraints: robocalls often encompass multiple legal jurisdictions of different countries/states, the large volume of robocalls, their multilingual nature, the lack of publicly available data, privacy concerns with obtaining data, etc. We present a study of international robocalls, aggregating robocall reports from countries across all inhabited continents and contribute by providing new findings on international robocalls from 65 different countries. We also present the first publicly available multimodal and international robocall dataset: 8.7 million call detail records, 839 robocall transcripts from 28 identified robocall campaign clusters, and 677 robocall recordings. We describe our methodology for collecting robocall data over a 9-month period and provide a detailed analysis comparing robocalls in the US with those in other countries. Our analysis covers several aspects, including uncovering calling patterns, identifying co-targeting attacks, discovering common robocall campaigns, extracting callback numbers, analyzing linguistic differences among robocalls in the same language but different regions, and other insights. Our results indicate that although robocalls are an international problem, the severity of the threat is significantly higher in the US than in other countries. We provide steps for future research and suggest remedies to reduce the effectiveness of robocalls based on our analysis.
tldr: This paper analyzes international robocall patterns and presents a multimodal dataset of robocalls from 65 countries.
motivation: Robocalls cause significant financial losses and are difficult to combat due to legal and practical constraints; the study aims to understand the international scope and characteristics of robocalls.
method: The authors collected 8.7 million call detail records, 839 transcripts, and 677 recordings over 9 months from multiple countries, and performed comparative analysis between US and non-US robocalls.
result: Robocalls are an international problem but the threat severity is significantly higher in the US than in other countries.
conclusion: The findings suggest that while robocalls are global, US-specific measures may be needed, and the dataset can support future research on combating robocalls.

title: Counting Small Induced Subgraphs: Hardness Of Symmetry-Based Properties
authors: Mingjun Liu Radu Curticapean
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jerrum and Meeks (TOCT, JCSS 2015) introduced the counting problems [MATH] for fixed graph properties [MATH]: Given an input graph [MATH] and [MATH], count the [MATH]-vertex subsets [MATH] such that the induced subgraph [MATH] satisfies [MATH]. For recursively enumerable [MATH], it is known that [MATH] is either #W[1]-hard or fixed-parameter tractable. A direct classification depending on [MATH] however still remains open. In particular, the status was open for the property of graphs without nontrivial automorphisms, also mentioned in a very recent survey on parameterized counting by Roth (Comput.~Sci.~Rev.~2026). This is a natural property that evades all currently known techniques for proving #W[1]-hardness, including a general toolkit based on Fourier analysis that was very recently introduced by Curticapean and Neuen (SODA~2025). In this paper, we show that counting induced [MATH]-vertex graphs without nontrivial automorphisms is #W[1]-hard by constructing ``clique scaffolds'', i.e., problem-specific restrictions of the property that enable a reduction from the [MATH]-clique problem. More generally, we show that for every finite group [MATH], counting [MATH]-vertex induced subgraphs with automorphism group [MATH] is #W[1]-hard.
tldr: This paper proves #W[1]-hardness of counting induced subgraphs with no nontrivial automorphisms, using clique scaffolds.
motivation: The problem of counting induced subgraphs with a given property is fundamental in parameterized complexity, and the status for the property of having no nontrivial automorphisms was open.
method: The authors construct 'clique scaffolds', which are problem-specific restrictions that enable a reduction from the k-clique problem.
result: Counting induced k-vertex subgraphs without nontrivial automorphisms is #W[1]-hard, and more generally, for any finite group G, counting induced subgraphs with automorphism group G is #W[1]-hard.
conclusion: The paper resolves an open problem in parameterized counting complexity, showing hardness for a natural symmetry-based property.

title: Labelled Sequent Calculi For Propositional Team Logics
authors: Fausto Barbero, Marianna Girlando, Valentin M\"uller, Fan Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Team semantics is a general framework where formulas are not interpreted with respect to a single point of evaluation, but with respect to sets of such points. Team semantics is used in dependence logic, to reason about dependencies between variables, and in inquisitive logic, to formalize the meaning of questions. We provide sound and complete labelled sequent calculi for four logics based on team semantics: basic inquisitive logic, propositional intuitionistic dependence logic, and their respective extensions with tensor disjunction. For technical reasons, we restrict ourselves to languages with finitely many propositional atoms. The rules of weakening, contraction and cut are shown to be admissible in each of our calculi. In the last part of the paper, we present terminating proof search procedures for variants of our proof systems, in which labels have a simplified structure.
tldr: The paper presents sound and complete labelled sequent calculi for propositional team logics, including inquisitive logic and dependence logic.
motivation: Team semantics provides a framework for reasoning about dependencies and questions, but proof-theoretic foundations for these logics were lacking.
method: The authors develop labelled sequent calculi for four team-based logics, prove admissibility of structural rules, and provide terminating proof search procedures.
result: Sound and complete labelled sequent calculi are obtained for basic inquisitive logic, propositional intuitionistic dependence logic, and their extensions with tensor disjunction.
conclusion: The work establishes a proof-theoretic foundation for team logics, enabling automated reasoning and further meta-theoretic studies.

title: Belief Contraction In Dynamic Epistemic Logic
authors: Snow Zhang Gaia Belardinelli (stanford University)
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic epistemic logic represents belief change via model transformations induced by epistemic events. Its standard formulation (Baltag, Moss, Solecki, 1998) provides a natural account of belief expansion through the elimination of possibilities, but it cannot model belief contraction about factual propositions. A classic response enriches Kripke models with plausibility orderings, representing contraction as an update that promotes certain possibilities over others. We show that this approach has expressive limitations. In particular, the approach cannot model belief that violates positive introspection and contraction dynamics in response to a hedged public announcement that phi might be false. Motivated by these considerations, we introduce a mechanism for belief contraction defined directly on standard Kripke models, without any constraints on the doxastic accessibility relation. We show that it satisfies some of the standard properties of belief contraction but not others, study the conditions under which contraction may be unsuccessful, and provide a sound and complete axiomatization of the logic via reduction axioms. We also define a more general dynamic logic that is an extension of standard DEL and accommodates belief contractions due to events such as private or semi-private announcements, and provide a complete and sound axiomatization of the general logic.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for belief contraction in dynamic epistemic logic, addressing limitations of existing approaches that rely on plausibility orderings.
motivation: Standard dynamic epistemic logic cannot model belief contraction about factual propositions, and existing solutions using plausibility orderings have expressive limitations, such as inability to model violations of positive introspection or hedged public announcements.
method: The authors introduce a belief contraction mechanism defined directly on standard Kripke models without constraints on the doxastic accessibility relation, and extend it to a general dynamic logic accommodating private or semi-private announcements, providing sound and complete axiomatizations via reduction axioms.
result: The proposed contraction satisfies some standard properties but not others; conditions for unsuccessful contraction are studied, and the logic is fully axiomatized.
conclusion: The work provides a novel approach to belief contraction in dynamic epistemic logic, but it is purely in the domain of philosophical logic and does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Most Properties Are Undecidable For Transitive Tense Logics
authors: Qian Chen (the Tsinghua-Uva JRC For Logic, Department Of Philosophy, Tsinghua University), Tenyo Takahashi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A logics' property is decidable in a class of logics if there exists an algorithm that decides whether a finitely axiomatizable logic in the class has the property. Many properties are undecidable for bimodal logics but decidable for linear tense logics, which leads to a general question on how the interactions of modalities affect the decidability of properties. In this paper, we study the decidability of properties for transitive tense logics and show that most properties are undecidable in the lattice NExt(K4t) of transitive tense logics, including Kripke completeness, the finite model property, and decidability. Our proof method adapts Chagrov's approach of constructing a reduction from an undecidable problem of Minsky machines to the decision problem for logics' properties, yielding a general scheme of proving the undecidability of these properties.
tldr: This paper proves undecidability of many properties for transitive tense logics using a reduction from Minsky machines.
motivation: To understand how interactions of modalities affect decidability of properties in bimodal logics, specifically transitive tense logics.
method: Adapts Chagrov's approach to construct a reduction from an undecidable problem of Minsky machines to the decision problem for logics' properties.
result: Shows that Kripke completeness, the finite model property, and decidability are undecidable in the lattice NExt(K4t) of transitive tense logics.
conclusion: Most properties are undecidable for transitive tense logics, extending known undecidability results from bimodal logics.

title: Labelled Sequents For Inquisitive First-Order Modal Logic
authors: Simone Conti Ivano Ciardelli (university Of Padua)
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent work, an inquisitive first-order modal logic has been proposed to reason about relations of modal dependence, including the notion of global supervenience (functional dependence among the extensions of predicates relative to a space of possibilities). At present, no proof system exists for this logic. We provide a complete labelled sequent calculus, extending a calculus developed by Litak and Sano for a weak version of inquisitive first-order logic. We prove strong completeness for the calculus and show that it enjoys desirable structural properties, including the invertibility of its rules and the admissibility of cut.
tldr: This paper presents a labelled sequent calculus for inquisitive first-order modal logic, focusing on proof theory and completeness.
motivation: Inquisitive first-order modal logic was proposed to reason about modal dependence and supervenience, but no proof system existed.
method: The authors extend a labelled sequent calculus by Litak and Sano, proving strong completeness and structural properties like invertibility and cut admissibility.
result: A complete labelled sequent calculus is provided with desirable structural properties.
conclusion: The calculus fills a gap in proof theory for inquisitive modal logic, but the work is purely logical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Intuitionistic Monotone Modal Logic: Proof Theory And Semantics
authors: Jim de Groot Tiziano Dalmonte
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recently introduced intuitionistic monotone modal logic IM. We first provide a semantic characterisation for a family of natural extensions of IM in terms of constructive neighbourhood models. We then present a calculus for IM and its extensions, obtained by adapting a structured calculus for the classical monotone modal logic M. Based on the calculus, we prove some preliminary results for IM, including its decidability. Our calculus also reveals an interesting analogy between constructive and intuitionistic variants of M and the corresponding variants of K, thereby further justifying IM as a faithful intuitionistic variant of M.
tldr: This paper studies intuitionistic monotone modal logic, providing a semantic characterization and a calculus for the logic and its extensions.
motivation: The authors aim to fill a gap in the study of intuitionistic modal logics by investigating the monotone variant, which has not been thoroughly explored.
method: They use constructive neighbourhood models for semantics and adapt a structured calculus from classical monotone modal logic to the intuitionistic setting.
result: They prove decidability for the basic logic and some extensions, and reveal an analogy between constructive and intuitionistic variants of monotone modal logic and the corresponding variants of normal modal logic.
conclusion: The work justifies intuitionistic monotone modal logic as a faithful intuitionistic counterpart of classical monotone modal logic, but the results are purely logical and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Minimal In Vitro Assay For Cell Intercalation Highlights The Importance Of Interfacial Tension And Migratory Forces
authors: Artur Ruppel
Vladimir Misiak
Sadjad Arzash
Daniel Selma-Herrador
Thomas Boudou
M. Lisa Manning
François Fagotto
Martial Balland
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies cell intercalation in a minimal in vitro system, focusing on mechanical forces and interfacial tension.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms driving cell intercalation, a key process in morphogenesis, is important for developmental biology.
method: A minimal assay with four cells was used to measure the roles of junction tension and migratory forces during intercalation.
result: Intercalation is driven by both interfacial tension and migratory forces, as demonstrated in the controlled in vitro system.
conclusion: The minimal system highlights the importance of mechanical forces in cell rearrangement, providing insights into tissue morphogenesis.

title: Temporally Super-resolved Dispersive Fourier Transformation Spectroscopy
authors: Qi Wen
Zhaoyang Wen
Yuan Chen
Bowen Sun
Zhicheng Huang
Ming Yan
Heping Zeng
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a temporally super-resolved dispersive Fourier transformation spectroscopy technique for single-shot measurement of non-repetitive spectra.
motivation: Conventional dispersive Fourier transformation spectroscopy has limited temporal resolution, preventing observation of ultrafast spectral dynamics.
method: The authors develop a super-resolved time-stretch spectroscopy method that sequentially measures non-repetitive spectra in a single shot.
result: Proof-of-concept experiments demonstrate the ability to resolve spectral evolution of 25-GHz electro-optic comb pulses and distinguish spectra separated by 3 ps.
conclusion: The technique enables temporally super-resolved spectroscopy for ultrafast phenomena.

title: Super-Snell Scanning Light-field Display For Ultrawide-angle High-resolution Glasses-free Three-dimensional Displays
authors: Yifan Chen

Tao Yu

Qionghai Dai
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a scanning light-field display achieving ultrawide viewing angle and high resolution using the Snell's window effect.
motivation: Glasses-free 3D displays suffer from limited viewing angle and resolution; the authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They design a super-Snell scanning light-field architecture that exploits Snell's window effect to expand the viewing angle.
result: The prototype demonstrates a 150° viewing angle and nearly 480-pixel resolution.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables glasses-free 3D displays with significantly improved performance.

authors: Ulrike Frühling

tldr: This is a correction notice for a paper on a terahertz-field-driven X-ray streak camera, which is an ultrafast measurement technique.
motivation: The original paper presented a method for single-shot X-ray pulse characterization using terahertz fields, relevant to ultrafast science.
method: The correction likely addresses errors or clarifications in the original publication.
result: No new results are presented; it is a minor correction.

title: Discovery Is Not The Opposite Of Application
authors: Hiranya V. Peiris
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper argues against framing research funding as a choice between discovery and application, using economic and evidence-based reasoning.
motivation: To correct misconceptions about the relationship between fundamental and applied research in funding decisions.
method: The author presents arguments from economics, evidence, and human perspectives to show that discovery and application are complementary.
result: The paper concludes that the dichotomy between discovery and application is false and harmful to research funding.
conclusion: Research funding should not force a choice between discovery and application; both are essential and interdependent.

title: Electrospray Ion Beam Deposition For Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy Of Complex Molecules
authors: Dhaneesh Kumar
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a method for depositing complex molecules onto surfaces for scanning tunnelling microscopy.
motivation: Imaging complex molecules with STM requires gentle deposition methods to avoid fragmentation.
method: Electrospray ion beam deposition is used to land intact molecules on a surface under vacuum.
result: The technique enables STM imaging of large, fragile molecules that are difficult to deposit otherwise.
conclusion: ES-IBD is a useful tool for molecular-scale imaging but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Loss Of Echs1 In Neural Stem And Progenitor Cells Impairs Neurogenesis Via Er Stress Activation And Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming
authors: Chun-Hui Duan

abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the role of ECHS1 in neural stem cells and its impact on neurogenesis through ER stress and lipid metabolic reprogramming.
motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying neurogenesis is crucial for brain development and potential therapies for neurological disorders.
method: The authors used conditional knockout mice to delete Echs1 in neural stem and progenitor cells and performed transcriptomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic analyses.

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.

tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects drive cell extrusion is important for tissue morphogenesis and homeostasis.
method: The authors develop a 3D bubbly vertex model to simulate curved epithelial sheets and analyze cell shape changes and extrusion events.
result: They find that cells at topological defects experience enhanced mechanical stress, leading to bulging and subsequent extrusion.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the role of geometry and mechanics in cell extrusion, relevant to developmental biology and disease.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding the hydrodynamics of microbial motility is important for biology and microfluidics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements around a free-swimming microalga.
result: Discovery of unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
conclusion: The findings expand understanding of microhydrodynamics with biological implications.

title: High-energy Emission From The Galactic Center
authors: Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, And Régis Terrier
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy astrophysical emission from the Galactic Center, focusing on the supermassive black hole and surrounding structures.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength overview of the Galactic Center's high-energy phenomena, including accretion, flares, and plasma bubbles.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths (X-ray, gamma-ray, etc.) and theoretical models.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of the Galactic Center's high-energy emission and its sources.
conclusion: The Galactic Center is a unique laboratory for studying high-energy astrophysics, with ongoing mysteries about its emission mechanisms.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Understanding charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating quantum chromodynamics (QCD) and exploring quark confinement.
method: The paper reviews experimental results from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: The review highlights recent advances from BESIII, which has become the leading facility for such measurements with high-precision data.
conclusion: The study of open-charm meson pairs provides valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its contributions to planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes the basics of planetary radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind for over two decades, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss marks the end of an era for ground-based planetary radar.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo 305-m radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo Observatory following its collapse in 2020.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific achievements across multiple decades and upgrades.
result: Highlights major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades enabled sustained scientific impact, and its legacy continues through successor facilities.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's incoherent scatter radar and other instruments.
motivation: To highlight the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric physics.
method: Review of key results from incoherent scatter radar, lidar, and optical measurements of the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
result: Summarizes advances in plasma physics, space weather, atomic metal layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory enabled unique observations of geospace phenomena, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers provide insights into turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, helping to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully explain the rapid transition.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, providing insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection and parameter estimation methods for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents the current state of gravitational wave predictions from supernovae and outlines multimessenger research strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from supernovae, combined with photons and neutrinos, will offer unique insights into the central engine and neutron star formation.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on large-scale structure surveys.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the matter distribution with the CMB dipole, which could reveal a fundamental inconsistency in the standard model of cosmology.
method: The authors analyze recent catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, comparing the observed dipole in their distribution with the CMB dipole, and review potential biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the ΛCDM model, but further investigation is needed to rule out systematic errors or alternative interpretations.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on dark matter halos.
motivation: Dark matter self-interactions are a key aspect of dark sector models, and astrophysical observations provide tests for these scenarios.
method: The review synthesizes results from galaxy to large-scale structure observations, comparing predictions of self-interacting dark matter models with data.
result: The paper summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections from various astrophysical probes.
conclusion: Astrophysical tests place important bounds on dark matter self-interactions, guiding future model-building and observations.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper is a review summarizing key advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, including experimental and modeling approaches.
result: It highlights the effects of turbulence, liquid rheology, and surfactants on bubble behavior, but no specific quantum-related results are presented.
conclusion: The review provides insights for modeling two-phase flows but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Propagation And Collisionless Damping Of Topologically-protected Surface Plasma Waves In Non-uniformly Magnetized Plasma Columns
authors: Roopendra Singh Rajawat And Gennady Shvets
abstract: Recent theoretical studies revealed the existence of topologically-protected surface plasma waves (TSPWs) in uniformly magnetized cold plasma columns. Reflections-free propagation of the TSPWs along arbitrarily-shaped plasma boundaries oriented perpendicularly to the magnetic field was shown to be preserved even when their collisionless damping by localized upper-hybrid resonances was accounted for. Here we extend this theory to the realistic case of three-dimensional magnetic field produced by finite-sized magnetic coils. We demonstrate that when TSPWs are launched in the direction of the decreasing magnetic field, they are collisionlessly absorbed within a highly localized (evanescent) region as they propagate away from the magnetic coil. We show that the resulting wave reflection can be negligible—in clear contrast with wave reflection from the corresponding evanescence regions of unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
tldr: This paper studies topologically-protected surface plasma waves in magnetized plasma columns, focusing on their propagation and collisionless damping in non-uniform magnetic fields.
motivation: To extend the theory of topologically-protected surface plasma waves from uniform to realistic three-dimensional magnetic fields, and to understand their absorption and reflection properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in a cold plasma column with a non-uniform magnetic field produced by finite-sized coils, using a model that accounts for collisionless damping by upper-hybrid resonances.
result: They find that waves launched in the direction of decreasing magnetic field are collisionlessly absorbed in a localized evanescent region, with negligible reflection, contrasting with unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
conclusion: The study demonstrates robust absorption of topologically-protected surface plasma waves in realistic magnetic field configurations, which may have implications for plasma heating or wave manipulation.

title: Search For Decays Of The Higgs Boson Into Pair-produced Pseudoscalar Particles Decaying Into Τ + ...
authors: The ATLAS Collaboration
abstract: A search for a pair of low-mass pseudoscalars that promptly decay into -leptons is presented using 140 fb of proton–proton collision data at TeV centre-of-mass energy recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The result is used to place constraints on exotic decays of the Higgs boson into four -leptons, . This search focuses on events with either one or two -leptons decaying into hadrons and neutrinos, and the remaining three or two -leptons decaying into either electron or muon and neutrinos. No significant excess is observed above the expected Standard Model background and upper limits at the 95% confidence level on are set ranging from 0.06 to 0.23, depending on the mass ranging from 15 to 60 GeV.
tldr: This paper reports an ATLAS search for Higgs boson decays into pseudoscalars decaying to tau leptons, finding no significant excess and setting upper limits.
motivation: To probe beyond-Standard-Model physics by searching for exotic Higgs decays to light pseudoscalars, which are predicted in many extensions of the Standard Model.
method: Analyzes 140 fb^-1 of proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector, selecting events with one or two hadronically decaying taus and the remaining taus decaying to electrons or muons.
result: No significant excess over the Standard Model background is observed; 95% CL upper limits on the branching ratio are set between 0.06 and 0.23 for pseudoscalar masses from 15 to 60 GeV.
conclusion: The results constrain exotic Higgs decays to four tau leptons, but do not provide evidence for new physics.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical gas sensing technique using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component gas detection.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.
method: The authors use two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers modulated at the same frequency with a 45° phase difference, co-exciting a quartz tuning fork. The piezoelectric signal is orthogonally demodulated via a lock-in amplifier to decouple the concentration information of two gases.
result: The sensor achieves excellent linear responses for methane and acetylene with low systematic errors (0.54% and 0.79%) and detection limits of 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, respectively.
conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection with a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling.

tldr: This paper presents a photosensitizer that selectively kills β-lactamase-expressing bacteria upon light activation, addressing antibiotic resistance.
motivation: Antibiotic resistance is a growing crisis driven by selective pressure; new strategies to kill resistant bacteria without affecting susceptible ones are needed.
method: The authors designed a compound that remains harmless until activated by β-lactamase, which is expressed by resistant bacteria, and then becomes a photosensitizer that produces reactive oxygen species upon light exposure.

motivation: Colorectal cancer is a major health challenge with poor prognosis; understanding mechanisms of ferroptosis could lead to new therapeutic strategies.
